question: Which surfaces can a first band on a loop of rings make while every contact stays persistent?

public_inputs.library: band_lib.py of BAND-SURFACE-20261108-001A (sha256 3061f2917a74f1510b929c85341e2ed1abe991d547c0fb549e180351d2ccc8ea), on GROW-NET-20261108-001A's grow_lib.
public_inputs.run: run.py in this folder, 8 worker processes.
public_inputs.family: Every rotation system of a loop of n rings plus one band of n rings: single rungs for n = 3 to 8, double rungs for n = 3 and 4.
public_inputs.exactness: Exact: return counts are followed until the next vector lies in the span of the earlier ones; no lag cutoff.

forbidden_inputs: Changing the family after seeing results
primary_observable: The balanced rotation systems by genus, face sizes and whether a flip fixes every contact.
cheapest_meaningful_control: BAND-SURFACE-20261108-001A's checks (the n x 2 torus is balanced) and GROW-NET-20261108-001A's exact test.
decision_or_followup_rule: H1, frozen: balanced first bands lie on the sphere only for single rungs at n = 4 (the cube). H2, frozen: with double rungs some balanced first band is the torus. If both hold, the first band's surface is mostly not a sphere, and which higher surfaces bands can grow is the next question.
stop_rule: Stop when every rotation system of the family has its verdict.
nonclaims: Exploratory: one band, these loop sizes.
feasibility_disclosure: Before freezing, a scratch run of the same family up to n = 7 (single) and n = 4 (double) gave exactly these patterns, so H1 and H2 are not blind predictions; n = 8 single rungs is new. run.py --pilot timed n = 3 and printed no verdicts.
